task:
IPRange needs a string constructor and range relations for DHCP pools and firewall ranges, which are usually not CIDR-aligned. This is a minor release, so every change must be additive.

- Widen the constructor to string|IPAddress $start, string|IPAddress $end. IPAddress instances passed in are stored as they are (start() returns the same object); invalid strings throw the IPAddress constructor's InvalidArgumentException. new IPRange(start: ..., end: ...) keeps working.
- containsRange(IPRange $other): bool, true when other lies within this range. Leave contains(string|IPAddress $ip) unchanged, parameter name included ($range->contains(ip: '10.0.0.1') must keep working).
- overlaps(IPRange $other): bool.
- intersection(IPRange $other): ?IPRange, the common range, or null when they are disjoint.
- isAdjacent(IPRange $other): bool, true when the ranges are disjoint and touch (one ends right before the other starts); overlapping ranges are not adjacent, as with Subnet::isAdjacent(). It must work for a range ending at 255.255.255.255.
- Do not accept Subnet parameters; callers convert with $subnet->addressRange(). Document the new methods and the widened constructor, with the changelog.
notes: Plan item 2 of the 5.3.0 plan; a 2026-11-08 Pair run on it stopped at the design stage.
